_meta.basis: TCCC MARCH-PAWS (USAF Pararescue PAWS extension, JSOM 2017) + JTS CoERCCC Joint En Route Care Guidelines FY26. Civilian XABCDE maps 1:1 (X=M, A, B=R, C, D=H-head, E=H-hypothermia/exposure).
_meta.why: Most potentially survivable trauma deaths are from hemorrhage, so M comes before A. The game's primary trauma framework and its scoring follow this order.

sequence.name: Scene safety / security
checks: scene safe or staged for PD/FD

sequence.name: Massive hemorrhage
checks: rapid blood sweep: head to toe incl. under the patient and groin/axilla
interventions: tourniquet (high and tight if unsure, then reassess and move 2–3 in above the wound)
second tourniquet if bleeding continues
hemostatic packing + 3 min firm pressure (junctional)
junctional tourniquet
pressure dressing

sequence.name: Airway
checks: talking? noisy? blood/vomit? facial trauma? burns?
interventions: position of comfort (sit up/lean forward with facial trauma)
recovery position
jaw thrust
suction
NPA (not with basilar skull/midface fx)
SGA
intubation (P/CC)
surgical cric for facial/airway trauma or failed airway
graded: supine positioning of a conscious facial-trauma patient

sequence.name: Respiration
checks: look for wounds, flail segment, paradoxical movement
interventions: vented chest seal on every open chest wound
needle decompression (5th ICS AAL or 2nd ICS MCL, 10–14g, ≥3.25 in) for suspected tension
finger thoracostomy (CC)
O2 titrated (SpO2 goal 92–96%; >93% with TBI)
BVM/CPAP for flail
graded: needle decompression into a herniated stomach (see diaphragm rupture)

sequence.name: Circulation
interventions: re-check every tourniquet and dressing
pelvic binder for suspected pelvic fracture
IV/IO access (2 lines)
whole blood / plasma:PRBC if available (CC)
calcium after first unit, then every 4 units
TXA 2 g IV/IO within 3 h of injury
permissive hypotension: radial pulse / SBP ~80–90 (BUT SBP ≥110 with TBI)
crystalloid only if no blood, small boluses

sequence.name: Hypothermia + Head injury
interventions: insulate from ground, remove wet clothing, hypothermia wrap, active warming torso/axillae with barrier
warm all fluids to 38 °C
TBI: SpO2 >93%, SBP >110, EtCO2 35–40 (38–42 per JTS), head up 30°, loosen collar
herniation: hypertonic saline 3% 250 mL; brief hyperventilation EtCO2 30–35 ONLY with herniation signs
graded: any SpO2 <90 or SBP <90 in TBI (each doubles mortality)

sequence.name: Pain
interventions: acetaminophen + meloxicam (mild/moderate, able to swallow)
ketamine 20 mg / 0.15–0.3 mg/kg slow IV or 50–100 mg IN/IM (moderate–severe, shock OK)
fentanyl 0.5–1 mcg/kg IV or 100 mcg IN
IO lidocaine before flush in a conscious patient
ondansetron for nausea
graded: no analgesia for a long-bone fracture

sequence.name: Antibiotics
interventions: TCCC FY26: cefadroxil 1 g PO (or cephalexin 500 mg PO) if able to swallow; ceftriaxone 2 g IV/IM/IO if not
ertapenem post-surgical / per protocol
open fracture: cefazolin early (civilian)
tetanus toxoid 0.5 mL IM if available
broad gram-negative + anaerobe coverage for bowel/fecal contamination
graded: no antibiotics for an open wound on a prolonged transport
beta-lactam given despite anaphylaxis on the history card
sequence.applies: Prolonged transport / austere / CC calls. Short urban transports: antibiotics at the ED are standard and not penalized.

sequence.name: Wounds
checks: full secondary sweep: log roll, armpits, groin, scalp, under jewelry
interventions: dress all wounds
moist dressing for evisceration/degloving
irrigate gross contamination
eye shield (no pressure) for open globe
burn care + rule-of-10 fluids if >20% TBSA
remove rings/jewelry before swelling
graded: rings left on a swelling hand

sequence.name: Splinting
interventions: splint fractures early (less bleeding and pain)
traction splint for isolated mid-shaft femur
splint as found unless pulseless (then gentle realignment once)
spinal motion restriction per criteria
avoid circumferential/constrictive splints
graded: compartment syndrome from a tight splint

sequence.name: Communicate & document
interventions: MIST report: Mechanism, Injuries, Signs (vitals), Treatment (incl. TQ times and drug times)
verify TQs, airway, chest seals at handoff
TCCC casualty card / PCR auto-built from the event log

reassessment: After any intervention or patient movement (log roll, loading, moving onto the stretcher), re-check M → A → R → C. Tourniquets loosen, chest seals fail, pneumos re-accumulate. The FTO grades reassessment frequency.

difficultyBehavior.L1: On-screen MARCH-PAWS checklist; the partner prompts the next step.
difficultyBehavior.L4+: No checklist; partner only does what you tell them.
